User

I want you to think super hard and design a super comprehensive and granular plan for me for a phenomenally impressive TUI using OpenTUI/ink and bun and typescript/react called phage-explorer. You’ll need to do exhaustive research on the web to figure out how to best make it. This should make it super easy and intuitive and user-friendly to browse through the various common types of phages, like lambda phages, with a single button press, like the down arrow. For each phage, the full screen TUI should show a mind blowingly slick and visually appears HUD UI showing key information about the phage, and it should look up from standard genetic databases the actual genetic code itself and display this in a standardized grid format that uses the full width of the available screen space efficiently and completely. Each letter ACTG should have a different color mapping where both the background color and foreground text color is a specific shade/hue (we can had themes the user can cycle through) to clearly present the code. The genetic data should be initially downloaded and cached locally in SQLite (we can use a wasm version of SQLite so that this whole thing can be displayed in a browser also; also see https://github.com/coder/ghostty-web and figure out how to use it for this). By pressing a single button the user should be able to toggle between ACTG view and codon view, where each 3 letter codon gets mapped to one of the 20 amino acids (using their standard one-letter abbreviations, with a helpful key presented in the corner that can be toggled on and off). Like with ACTG, each of the 20 amino acid letters and stop signal should have their own specific coloring, the point is to be able to convey with color at a glance the full genetic code for a particular phage with no latency. So that by pressing the down key the user can instantly move between phages and see what’s the same and what’s different using color. Another amazing feature would be to find 3d models of the actual phages, like the lambda phages icosahedral capsid and little injector claw mechanism on the web in standard formats and download and cache them and then render them in the corner in a little square in the hud using a Unicode renderer that shows them slowly rotating.

Assistant

Here’s a full design for phage-explorer, with enough structure that you can basically go implement it from here.

0. Big-picture goals & assumptions

Assumptions I’m making:

  • You want a real, full-screen TUI written in TypeScript/React on Bun, using OpenTUI (@opentui/react) as the primary renderer and optionally Ink as a secondary renderer.

  • Phage genomes are pulled from standard databases: primarily NCBI GenBank / RefSeq (e.g. lambda phage RefSeq NC_001416.1, ~48.5 kb dsDNA) with optional ENA / PhagesDB support.

  • Sequences are cached locally into SQLite, and you want a WASM SQLite variant in the browser using the official sqlite3 WASM module or ES-module wrappers like @sqlite.org/sqlite-wasm / @sqliteai/sqlite-wasm, ideally backed by OPFS for persistence.

  • Phage 3D structure is sourced from RCSB PDB / EMDB (e.g. lambda capsid 7VI9, tail/portal 8K35/8K39) and/or educational models (Sketchfab etc.), then converted into a simplified model your Unicode renderer can animate.

  • Browser version should feel like “the same TUI”, using ghostty-web (xterm.js API-compatible WASM terminal) where appropriate.

Everything below is structured to keep domain logic shared and swap renderers / environments cleanly.

1. Project layout / architecture

Use a Bun monorepo (via bun workspace) with clear layering:

nix
phage-explorer/
  packages/
    core/           # domain logic, codon translation, theming, 3D projection
    data-pipeline/  # build-time tools: fetch from NCBI/ENA/PhagesDB, build phage.db
    db-runtime/     # DB abstraction over native SQLite (Bun) and WASM SQLite
    tui-opentui/    # main CLI TUI using @opentui/react
    tui-ink/        # optional Ink-based frontend, same React component tree
    renderer-3d/    # shared math + ASCII/braille renderer
    web-standalone/ # browser UI using sqlite-wasm + DOM, mimicking TUI layout
    web-terminal/   # browser ghostty-web front-end talking to a real TUI over PTY

Separation of concerns:

  • core: pure TypeScript (no Node, no DB):

    • DNA / AA types & codon tables

    • translation & reading-frame logic

    • theming/color maps for nucleotides & amino acids

    • utility to turn sequences into “grid slices” given viewport

    • 3D math: projections, rotations, simple shading

  • db-runtime: abstract DB interface + implementations:

    • PhageRepository interface (list phages, get genome, get models, etc.)

    • BunSqliteRepository using Bun’s SQLite / bun:sqlite

    • WasmSqliteRepository using @sqlite.org/sqlite-wasm or @sqliteai/sqlite-wasm with OPFS-backed persistence.

  • data-pipeline: Node/Bun scripts for building the SQLite DB from public APIs:

    • NCBI E-utilities + NCBI Virus portal, ENA Browser API, and PhagesDB API.

  • tui-opentui: actual phage-explorer CLI; uses @opentui/react as the React renderer and db-runtime as data source; all UI is React components.

  • tui-ink: same React component tree, but rendered with Ink; this gives access to Ink’s component ecosystem (ink-box, ink-gradient, ink-picture, etc.).

  • renderer-3d: small engine turning 3D models into Unicode “frames” (ASCII or braille/half-blocks) that a TUI component can just print.

  • web-standalone: React+Vite app that:

    • loads sqlite3 WASM from the official module

    • opens an OPFS-backed DB

    • uses the same core & renderer-3d to render a graphical-but-TUI-ish layout in the browser (no real terminal required)

  • web-terminal:

    • uses ghostty-web to embed a VT100 terminal in the DOM

    • connects over WebSocket to a server-side Bun process running tui-opentui attached to a PTY

    • this gives a “real TUI in browser” experience for remote or heavy-data use

That gives you:

  • Local CLI with native SQLite

  • Browser “local-first” app with sqlite-wasm

  • Browser “remote terminal” mode via ghostty-web

2. Data model & SQLite schema

2.1. Phage catalog

Seed a curated list of phages (lambda, T4, T7, ΦX174, MS2, etc.) and expand from NCBI Virus / PhagesDB.

phage table:

sql

pgsql
CREATE TABLE phage (
  id                 TEXT PRIMARY KEY, -- slug, e.g. "lambda"
  display_name       TEXT NOT NULL,    -- "Escherichia phage lambda"
  family             TEXT,             -- e.g. "Caudoviricetes"
  genus              TEXT,             -- e.g. "Lambdavirus"
  host               TEXT,             -- "Escherichia coli K-12"
  baltimore_group    TEXT,             -- e.g. "I" (dsDNA) :contentReference[oaicite:11]{index=11}
  genome_length_bp   INTEGER NOT NULL, -- 48502 for lambda
  genome_type        TEXT NOT NULL,    -- "dsDNA", "ssDNA", etc.
  refseq_accession   TEXT,             -- e.g. "NC_001416.1" :contentReference[oaicite:12]{index=12}
  genbank_accession  TEXT,             -- e.g. "J02459.1" :contentReference[oaicite:13]{index=13}
  gc_content         REAL,
  num_genes          INTEGER,          -- e.g. ~73 coding for lambda :contentReference[oaicite:14]{index=14}
  tags               TEXT              -- JSON: {common:true, temperate:true,...}
);

2.2. Sequences & annotations

sequence table (for now: one main DNA sequence per phage):

sql

pgsql
CREATE TABLE sequence (
  phage_id       TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES phage(id),
  source         TEXT NOT NULL, -- "refseq", "genbank", "phagesdb"
  accession      TEXT NOT NULL,
  format         TEXT NOT NULL, -- "fasta" or "genbank"
  length_bp      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  seq            TEXT NOT NULL, -- uppercase ACTG... (possibly compressed at rest)
  md5            TEXT NOT NULL,
  fetched_at     INTEGER NOT NULL, -- unix timestamp
  raw_metadata   TEXT             -- JSON: NCBI header, etc.
);

feature table for coding sequences and interesting landmarks (cos site, terminases, etc.):

sql

pgsql
CREATE TABLE feature (
  id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  phage_id      TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES phage(id),
  locus_tag     TEXT,
  gene          TEXT,
  product       TEXT,
  start_bp      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  end_bp        INTEGER NOT NULL,
  strand        INTEGER NOT NULL, -- +1 / -1
  frame         INTEGER,          -- 1,2,3 w.r.t + strand
  type          TEXT,             -- "CDS", "promoter", "terminator"
  qualifiers    TEXT              -- JSON bag for GenBank qualifiers
);

Codon-usage summary (to drive HUD graphs quickly):

sql

css
CREATE TABLE codon_usage (
  phage_id      TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES phage(id),
  aa_counts     TEXT NOT NULL, -- JSON: { "A": 1234, "R": 567, ... }
  codon_counts  TEXT NOT NULL  -- JSON: { "ATG": 10, "TTT": 23, ... }
);

3D models metadata:

sql

pgsql
CREATE TABLE model3d (
  id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  phage_id      TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES phage(id),
  role          TEXT NOT NULL,  -- "capsid", "tail", "full_virion"
  source        TEXT NOT NULL,  -- "pdb", "sketchfab", "custom"
  source_id     TEXT,           -- e.g. "7VI9", "8K35", or URL slug :contentReference[oaicite:15]{index=15}
  local_path    TEXT,           -- inside repo or OPFS
  vertices_blob BLOB,           -- preprocessed normalized vertices/triangles
  meta          TEXT            -- JSON for citation, resolution, etc.
);

Settings:

sql

pgsql
CREATE TABLE settings (
  key   TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  value TEXT NOT NULL
);

3. Data ingestion pipeline

All of this lives in packages/data-pipeline.

3.1. Fetching sequences

Primary pipeline:

  1. Take phage list from phage_catalog.json.

  2. For each phage where sequence row is missing or stale:

    • Use NCBI E-utilities (esearch+efetch) on nuccore with refseq_accession (e.g. NC_001416.1).

    • Request FASTA or GenBank format; parse into plain sequence + feature list.

  3. For phages better represented in PhagesDB (Actinobacteriophages), use its JSON API to obtain sequences & metadata.

  4. Optionally support ENA Browser API as alternative or fallback, e.g. for EMBL-format records.

All of this is build-time (or offline phage-explorer sync command) so that the TUI never goes to network for normal usage.

3.2. Precomputation

For each phage:

  • Compute GC content, base counts.

  • Pre-translate three reading frames using the standard bacterial genetic code (translation table 11).

  • Summarize aa_counts and codon_counts into JSON stored in codon_usage.

  • Optionally precompute a “canonical frame” (e.g. frame of the longest CDS covering most of genome) for quick AA view.

You can keep actual AA sequences out of DB and recompute on the fly, but precomputing is cheap (~50k bp → ~16.6k aa for lambda) so caching at rest is reasonable.

4. SQLite runtime: native vs WASM

4.1. Interface

In db-runtime, define a small interface:

ts

typescript
export interface PhageRepository {
  listPhages(): Promise<PhageSummary[]>;
  getPhageByIndex(index: number): Promise<PhageFull>; // includes seq, usage, features, models
  getPhageById(id: string): Promise<PhageFull>;
  prefetchAround(index: number, radius: number): Promise<void>;
}

Plus a DatabaseClient abstraction that wraps raw SQLite queries.

4.2. Native (Bun) implementation

  • Use Bun’s built-in SQLite driver (e.g. new Database("phage.db")); Bun supports .wasm too, but for CLI you want the native path.

  • Open DB read-only by default for robustness.

  • Use prepared statements for most queries; keep connections global.

4.3. Browser implementation with sqlite-wasm

For web-standalone and potentially web-embedded logic:

  • Use official SQLite WASM module as ES module (@sqlite.org/sqlite-wasm) or the wrapper @sqliteai/sqlite-wasm if you like the worker API.

  • Load DB either:

    • From a pre-built phage.db shipped as static asset + sqlite-wasm-http VFS (read-only over HTTP)

    • Or by seeding an empty OPFS DB then hydrating from a compressed JSON or SQL script.

Use OPFS for persistence so the user can download extra phages once and keep them across sessions.

WasmSqliteRepository implements the same PhageRepository API, so core + renderer-3d + UI code stays identical.

5. Core domain logic

All in packages/core:

5.1. Types

  • Nucleotide = 'A' | 'C' | 'G' | 'T' | 'N'

  • AminoAcid = 'A' | 'R' | ... | 'Y' | 'V' | '*' (STOP)

  • PhageSummary, PhageFull, Feature, etc.

5.2. Codon maps

  • Hard-code standard DNA codon → AA mapping from the DNA codon table (translation table 1 / bacterial nuclear code).

  • Provide:

ts

php
translateFrame(seq: string, frame: 0 | 1 | 2): string; // aa string
sliceNucleotides(seq: string, offset: number, length: number): string;
sliceAAs(aaSeq: string, codonOffset: number, lengthAA: number): string;

5.3. Grid slicer

Given:

  • viewportCols, viewportRows

  • hudHeight, footerHeight

  • mode: 'dna' | 'aa'

  • frame: 0 | 1 | 2

Compute:

  • rows = viewportRows - hudHeight - footerHeight - maybe3DHeight

  • For DNA view: basesPerRow = viewportCols

  • For AA view: aasPerRow = viewportCols

Return data structure like:

ts

typescript
type GridChar = {
  ch: string;          // "A" or "M"
  pos: number;         // base index or aa index
  diff?: 'same' | 'different' | 'gap';
};

type GridRow = { rowIndex: number; cells: GridChar[] };

function buildGrid(
  seqOrAa: string,
  startIndex: number,
  rows: number,
  cols: number
): GridRow[];

core doesn’t know about colors; it only knows positions and content.

6. Theming & color system

You want 2 color maps:

  • Nucleotide colors (ACTG + N)

  • AA colors (20 AAs + STOP)

Define:

ts

elm
type ColorPair = { fg: string; bg: string };

type NucleotideTheme = Record<Nucleotide, ColorPair>;
type AminoTheme = Record<AminoAcid, ColorPair>;

type HudTheme = {
  bg: string;
  text: string;
  accent1: string;
  accent2: string;
  dim: string;
  diffHighlight: string;
};

type Theme = {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  nucleotides: NucleotideTheme;
  aminoAcids: AminoTheme;
  hud: HudTheme;
};

Populate a few defaults:

  • “Spectrum”: A/C/G/T mapped to distinct hues, e.g. A–greenish, C–blue, G–yellow, T–red.

  • “Purine/Pyrimidine”: color-coded by chemical class, with intensity encoding GC vs AT.

  • “AA property”: amino acids grouped by hydrophobicity / charge and colored accordingly; STOP is bright white-on-red.

core exposes a ThemeManager that cycles themes, persists current theme via settings table.

7. TUI UX & layout (OpenTUI/Ink)

7.1. Screen layout

Design for 80x24 up to 200x60+; layout adapts based on auto-detected size.

Layout roughly:

css
┌─────────────────────────────── HUD (3–4 lines) ────────────────────────────────┐
│ [Phage name] [host] [family] [genome len] [GC%] [mode: DNA/AA] [frame]        │
│ [RefSeq acc] [source DB] [#genes] [selected theme]                            │
│ [diff vs: lambda] [position: 12,345 / 48,502 bp]                              │
├───────── Phage list / metadata ───┬──────────── DNA/AA grid ──────────────────┤
│ λ  Lambda (E. coli)              │ ACTGACTGACTG… colored by base              │
│ →T4  Enterobacteria phage T4     │ …                                          │
│   T7                             │ …                                          │
│   ΦX174                          │ …                                          │
│                                  │ …                                          │
│  3D ASCII phage block            │                                           │
│   (rotating capsid & tail)      │                                           │
├──────────────────────────────────┴───────────── Key / AA legend ──────────────┤
│ ↑/↓ phage  ←/→ scroll  v toggle DNA/AA  f frame  t theme  d diff  m 3D  ? help│
│ [optional AA legend: M Met, F Phe, ... with colors]                          │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

7.2. Keybindings

  • Up/Down: move selection in phage list; switching phages is instant if data prefetched.

  • Left/Right: scroll horizontally within sequence.

  • PgUp/PgDn: jump by one viewport page.

  • Home/End: jump to start/end.

  • v or Space: toggle DNA vs AA (codon) view.

  • f: cycle reading frame (1,2,3).

  • d: toggle diff mode vs reference phage.

  • t: cycle theme.

  • m: toggle/pause 3D rotation.

  • ? / h: toggle help overlay (AA legend, keymap).

  • /: fuzzy search phage by name/host.

7.3. React component structure

Rough component tree:

tsx

xml
<App>
  <LayoutManager>  // computes dimensions from OpenTUI/Ink APIs
    <HudBar />
    <Body>
      <Sidebar>
        <PhageList />
        <PhageStats />
        <Phage3DView />  // rotating ASCII
      </Sidebar>
      <MainPanel>
        <SequenceGrid />  // uses core.buildGrid + theme colors
      </MainPanel>
    </Body>
    <Footer>
      <KeyHints />
      <AALegend /> // togglable
    </Footer>
  </LayoutManager>
</App>

You can wrap this once and render via:

  • @opentui/react in tui-opentui

  • ink in tui-ink

To support both renderers without forking all components:

  • Define your own primitives: <TBox>, <TText>, <TKeyHandler>, etc.

  • Provide two adapters implementing those primitives with OpenTUI or Ink.

8. DNA vs codon (AA) view

8.1. DNA (ACTG) view

  • Each character is 1 column; rows sized to viewport width.

  • SequenceGrid asks core for GridRow[] for the current base index.

  • For each GridRow, you group sequences of identical colors into segments to reduce React node count:

ts

elm
type ColoredSegment = { text: string; colorPair: ColorPair };
  • Each row renders as a Box with a series of <TText> segments.

Base-level coloring:

  • simple mapping: A → theme.nucleotides.A, etc.

  • optionally lighten/darken background based on base index modulo 3 to hint codon boundaries.

8.2. Codon / AA view

  • SequenceGrid switches to AA mode:

    • For each phage, you keep precomputed aaFrame[0..2] in memory (or compute lazily and cache).

    • Each column is one AA character; each row is viewportCols characters; startAAIndex is derived from base index + frame.

  • AA letters are colored by theme.aminoAcids[aa].

  • Transparent framing: you may overlay faint vertical lines or lighten backgrounds every 5 or 10 AAs to help visual grouping.

8.3. Reading frames & ORF awareness

  • Default: display frame 1 from position 0 (canonical for lambda’s main ORF), but allow user to cycle frames.

  • Optionally, overlay Feature boundaries:

    • Underline or box segments where a CDS spans, with product names shown in a minimal overlay.

    • You can highlight currently focused gene in HUD, with coordinates and product.

8.4. AA key overlay

A small box in bottom-right when legendVisible:

  • Multi-row list like:

    • H (His) – basic

    • E (Glu) – acidic

    • etc., grouped by property, using the same colors as in the grid.

  • Toggle with ? or k.

9. Diff mode

Goal: user presses d, selects a reference phage (default lambda), then uses ↑/↓ to flip between phages and visually see differences.

Simplest version:

  • Only diff phages with the same length; show warning if lengths differ.

  • Precompute for each phage pair (or on-demand): mismatchBitset along sequence.

  • In DNA view:

    • When diff mode is on, SequenceGrid checks for mismatches at each index:

      • If same: optionally dim background or border.

      • If different: use hud.diffHighlight for background and keep the base letter/color for that phage.

  • In AA view:

    • Do the same but on AA index instead; differences in codons that are synonymous may show as same AA but diff DNA; you can allow toggling between “DNA diff” and “AA diff.”

More advanced: for unequal-length genomes, you can plug in a light alignment algorithm (global or local), but that’s a later phase.

10. 3D phage ASCII/Unicode renderer

10.1. Data sources

For each phage:

  • Prefer whole-capsid or tail reconstructions from PDB/EMDB when available, e.g. lambda capsid 7VI9, tail/portal 8K35/8K39.

  • Fallback: educational OBJ/STL models (e.g. “Lambda Bacteriophage Capsid - 3D Printable” on Sketchfab, bacteriophage models on TurboSquid/Free3D).

Preprocessing script (one-time):

  • Reads PDB/OBJ.

  • Normalizes coordinates into a unit sphere centered at origin.

  • Downsamples vertices and/or generates a coarse mesh (e.g. 1–2k triangles).

  • Stores as JSON/CBOR or BLOB in model3d.vertices_blob.

10.2. The renderer

In renderer-3d:

  • Implement a minimal 3D pipeline (can crib from existing ASCII renderer examples as inspiration).

  • Steps per frame:

    1. Take rotation angles rx, ry, rz (functions of time).

    2. Apply rotation matrix to vertices.

    3. Project onto 2D plane using perspective or orthographic projection.

    4. Map projected points into a small grid (say 24x16 cells).

    5. For each cell, compute:

      • nearest depth

      • value to encode as brightness

      • choose a Unicode char:

        • simplest: .:-=+*#%@ intensity ramp

        • fancier: braille / half-block characters with fg/bg color from shading (like “rich pixels”).

  • Output: an array of text rows ready for <TText>.

<Phage3DView> component:

  • On mount, sets up a timer (e.g. 10–20 fps).

  • Each tick updates an internal frame state and recomputes text region via renderer-3d.

  • On unmount/toggle, cancels timer.

  • Exposes keys m to pause/resume rotation and ,/. to slow/speed.

Keep the ASCII block relatively small (e.g. 30x18 char box) to avoid starving layout.

11. Browser story

You want both “local-in-browser” and “real terminal in browser”.

11.1. web-standalone (local WASM, DOM UI)

  • Vite + React, no terminal emulator.

  • On load:

    • Initialize sqlite3 WASM using the official HOWTO (three-step: load module, open DB, choose VFS).

    • Open phage.db in memory or OPFS; if DB missing, fetch it over HTTP + sqlite-wasm-http or re-run ingest client-side (not ideal for NCBI quotas).

  • Instantiate WasmSqliteRepository and pass into the same App React tree as in tui-opentui, but swap the renderer layer to DOM components (e.g. <div> equivalents of <TBox>).

  • Layout is visually identical to TUI but may use more subtle styling (rounded corners, CSS grid).

This mode uses the same sequence + 3D rendering logic and feels like a high-fidelity simulator of your TUI.

11.2. web-terminal (ghostty-web + remote TUI)

For a “true TUI in browser” experience:

  • Create a small backend server:

    • Bun HTTP server that spawns phage-explorer process under a PTY (e.g. using node-pty equivalent or Bun’s PTY APIs if available).

    • Bridge PTY input/output over WebSocket.

  • In web-terminal React app:

    • Use ghostty-web to instantiate a Terminal instance in the browser.

    • Hook term.onData(data => ws.send(data)) and ws.onmessage(ev => term.write(ev.data)) (exact pattern from ghostty-web README).

  • The backend process runs tui-opentui with native SQLite; this is ideal for remote HPC setups or big local datasets.

You can expose both modes in the same web app:

  • “Local mode” → sqlite-wasm + DOM layout

  • “Remote TUI mode” → ghostty-web terminal to a remote Bun process

12. Performance / “no latency” behavior

To keep “down-arrow phage flipping” instant:

  1. Eager preload:

    • After opening DB, PhageRepository prefetches PhageFull for the first N phages (say 20) into memory.

    • When the user is on index i, background task prefetches [i-5, i+5] ring; this ensures neighbors are almost always in RAM.

  2. In-memory representations:

    • For loaded phages, store:

      • raw DNA string

      • aaFrame[0..2] arrays

      • codon stats

    • SequenceGrid uses slices of these precomputed arrays only; no DB queries on scroll.

  3. Efficient rendering:

    • Only render visible rows; core.buildGrid is O(rows * cols) per redraw.

    • Avoid per-character React components: segment by color.

  4. Throttle updates:

    • When holding down arrow keys, avoid recomputing 3D view each time; 3D component drives its own update, while sequence view just swaps data.

  5. Async DB / WASM:

    • In the browser, run sqlite-wasm on a worker (per docs / WASM cookbook) to avoid blocking the main thread.

13. Implementation roadmap

A practical “do this in order” list:

  1. Bootstrapping

    • bun create tui phage-explorer (OpenTUI starter) and set up workspaces.

    • Add core, db-runtime, data-pipeline, and tui-opentui packages.

  2. DB + ingest

    • Implement data-pipeline scripts to build phage.db from a small initial phage set (lambda, T4, T7, ΦX174, MS2). Use NCBI E-utilities / PhagesDB for sequences and metadata.

    • Precompute codon usage.

  3. Core domain

    • Implement codon tables, translation, grid-building, theming.

  4. Basic TUI

    • Hook up tui-opentui with minimal layout: phage list + nucleotide grid; arrow-key navigation only.

    • Confirm performance on lambda’s 48.5kb genome.

  5. AA / codon view

    • Add translation & frame toggling.

    • Add AA legend overlay.

  6. Themes

    • Define at least 3 theme presets; implement theme-cycling and persistence.

  7. Diff mode

    • Add basic same-length diff vs reference phage (lambda by default).

  8. 3D renderer

    • Implement renderer-3d with a test cube.

    • Integrate with TUI; then plug in one real lambda model (PDB or educational OBJ) via preprocessor.

  9. Browser local mode

    • Build web-standalone with sqlite-wasm; wire to core and mimic TUI layout on DOM.

  10. ghostty-web mode

    • Build web-terminal that connects to backend PTY using ghostty-web; confirm phantom-less TUI behavior in browser.

  11. Polish

    • Add phage search, filter by host/family, export snapshots, etc.

    • Add config file support and “profiles” of phages (e.g. “classic teaching phages”, “giant phages”, etc.).

If you want next steps, the natural follow-up is: pick the first “vertical slice” (probably: lambda-only, DNA-only, no 3D) and I can lay out concrete types and module boundaries tailored to how you like to structure TS projects.

I have designed this architecture to be isomorphic—meaning the exact same TypeScript/React code will run natively in your terminal (via Bun) and in any web browser (via WebAssembly), providing a "sci-fi bio-HUD" experience with zero latency. 🧬 Phage-Explorer: The Master Plan 1. Executive Summary Phage-Explorer is a terminal-based bioinformatics visualization tool. It treats the terminal not as a command line, but as a high-fidelity graphics surface. • Core Stack: Bun (Runtime), TypeScript (Logic), React + Ink (UI Rendering). • Data Engine: SQLite (Native) + SQLite WASM (Browser) for instant lookups. • Visuals: Custom ASCII 3D Rasterization engine & Virtualized DNA Scrolling. • Web Target: Uses xterm.js (styled to match the Ghostty aesthetic) to render the React Ink output in the browser. 2. Architecture & Tech Stack We will use a Monorepo structure to separate the core logic from the platform-specific entry points. The Stack Component Technology Why? Runtime Bun Instant startup time (crucial for CLI tools) and built-in SQLite support. UI Framework React + Ink Ink is the industry standard for React-based TUIs. We use it to manage complex Flexbox layouts in the terminal. Data Layer Drizzle ORM A lightweight TypeScript ORM. It lets us write one schema that works on both bun:sqlite and sqlite-wasm. 3D Engine Three.js (Math Only) We use Three.js solely for matrix math (Vector3, Quaternions) and write a custom "ASCII Rasterizer" to project points to text characters. Web Terminal Xterm.js Note on Ghostty: coder/ghostty-web is currently the source for their marketing site, not a standalone library. We will use xterm.js but theme it to replicate Ghostty's beautiful padding, font rendering, and colors. Project Structure /phage-explorer
├── packages/
│ ├── core/ # Shared Business Logic
│ │ ├── components/ # Ink Components (HUD, Grid, 3DViewer)
│ │ ├── db/ # Drizzle Schema & Abstracted Client
│ │ ├── engine/ # 3D ASCII Projection Logic
│ │ └── state/ # Zustand Store (Navigation, Selection)
│ ├── cli/ # Native Entry Point (Bun)
│ │ └── index.tsx # Renders to process.stdout
│ └── web/ # Browser Entry Point (Vite)
│ └── index.tsx # Renders to Xterm.js stream
├── assets/ # 3D Models (.obj) & Seed DB
└── scripts/ # Data ingestion tools
3. The "Mind-Blowing" Features A. The Infinite Genetic Grid (Virtualized) Rendering 48,000 characters (the size of the Lambda phage genome) will lag if done naively. We will use Virtual Windowing. • Logic: We only render the ~20 rows of text visible on the screen. • State: A scrollOffset integer tracks how deep into the genome we are. • Optimization: Instead of rendering thousands of React components, we pre-assemble entire lines as strings using ANSI escape codes directly. This ensures 60 FPS scrolling. B. The "Defragmentation" Color Map We map the genetic code to specific hues to create a dense, visual data texture. • Nucleotide Mode (ACTG): • A (Adenine): Neon Green (#39FF14) • C (Cytosine): Cyan (#00FFFF) • G (Guanine): Amber (#FFBF00) • T (Thymine): Crimson (#DC143C) • Codon Mode (Amino Acids): • We toggle the view to group letters by 3 (e.g., ATG). • Use the RasMol color scheme (grouping amino acids by properties: Polar, Non-polar, Acidic, etc.). • Stop Codons (TAA, TAG, TGA) pulse with a red background. C. 3D ASCII Holo-Projector To render the icosahedral capsid of a phage in a terminal: 1 Loader: Load a low-poly .obj file of the phage structure. 2 Projection: For every frame, rotate the 3D vertices using a rotation matrix. 3 Rasterization: Project 3D points (x, y, z) to 2D terminal coordinates (row, col). 4 Shading: Calculate the "density" of points or surface normals to choose a character: (empty) \to . \to : \to + \to # \to @ (solid). 4. Implementation Steps Phase 1: Setup & Data Ingestion We need data before we can build the UI. 1 Initialize: bun init 2 Database: Create a phages.db SQLite file. 3 Ingest Script: Write a script to fetch the "Big 5" phages from the NCBI Nucleotide API and PhagesDB. • Download Lambda, T4, T7, M13, PhiX174. • Store them in the genomes table. • Self-contained: We ship this .db file with the app so it works offline immediately. Phase 2: The Core UI (React Ink) Create the HUD layout using Flexbox. // src/components/App.tsx

{/\* List of Phages \*/} {/\* The Matrix View \*/} {/\* 3D Model & Stats \*/}

Rotate const rotated = applyRotation(vertex, angle); // 2. Project const x = Math.floor(rotated.x \* scale + center.x); const y = Math.floor(rotated.y \* scale + center.y); // 3. Draw if (inBounds(x, y)) buffer\[y\]\[x\] = '#'; } return bufferToString(buffer); } Phase 4: The Browser Bridge (Ghostty/Web) To run this in the browser, we trick Ink into thinking it's running in a terminal. 1 Vite Setup: Create a new Vite app in packages/web. 2 Polyfills: Install vite-plugin-node-polyfills (Ink needs process.stdout). 3 Xterm.js Shim: import { Terminal } from '@xterm/xterm'; import { render } from 'ink';

This plan provides the granular steps, the architectural decisions, and the "wow" factors needed to make Phage-Explorer a reality. — Here is opus 4.5: Phage Explorer: Comprehensive Design Document Executive Summary Phage Explorer is a phenomenally impressive Terminal User Interface (TUI) application for browsing, visualizing, and analyzing bacteriophage genetic data. Built with Ink (React for CLIs), Bun, and TypeScript, it provides an immersive, full-screen HUD experience for exploring phage genomes with instant navigation, stunning color-coded sequence visualization, and optional 3D model rendering. The application also supports browser deployment via ghostty-web for broader accessibility. Data Layer 3.1 SQLite Schema -- Core phage information CREATE TABLE phages ( id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, name TEXT NOT NULL, accession TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, family TEXT, host TEXT, genome_length INTEGER, gc_content REAL, morphology TEXT, -- 'siphovirus', 'myovirus', 'podovirus', 'filamentous' lifecycle TEXT, -- 'lytic', 'lysogenic', 'chronic' description TEXT, ncbi_id TEXT, pdb_ids TEXT, -- JSON array of PDB structure IDs last_updated DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ); -- Full genetic sequences (stored in chunks for performance) CREATE TABLE sequences ( id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, phage_id INTEGER NOT NULL, chunk_index INTEGER NOT NULL, sequence TEXT NOT NULL, -- 10,000 bp per chunk FOREIGN KEY (phage_id) REFERENCES phages(id), UNIQUE(phage_id, chunk_index) ); -- Gene annotations CREATE TABLE genes ( id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, phage_id INTEGER NOT NULL, name TEXT, start_pos INTEGER NOT NULL, end_pos INTEGER NOT NULL, strand TEXT CHECK(strand IN ('+', '-')), product TEXT, FOREIGN KEY (phage_id) REFERENCES phages(id) ); -- 3D model cache CREATE TABLE models ( id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, phage_id INTEGER NOT NULL, pdb_id TEXT NOT NULL, model_data BLOB, -- Cached OBJ/STL data ascii_frames TEXT, -- Pre-rendered ASCII animation frames (JSON) FOREIGN KEY (phage_id) REFERENCES phages(id) ); -- User preferences CREATE TABLE preferences ( key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT ); -- Indexes for performance CREATE INDEX idx_phages_family ON phages(family); CREATE INDEX idx_sequences_phage ON sequences(phage_id); CREATE INDEX idx_genes_phage ON genes(phage_id); CREATE INDEX idx_genes_position ON genes(phage_id, start_pos, end_pos); 3.2 Pre-Seeded Phage Catalog The application ships with a curated list of "https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils"; interface NCBIConfig { email: string; // Required by NCBI apiKey?: string; // For higher rate limits tool: string; } class NCBIService { private config: NCBIConfig = { email: "phage-explorer@example.com", tool: "phage-explorer" }; /** * Fetch complete genome sequence in FASTA format */ async fetchGenome(accession: string): Promise { const url = new URL(${NCBI_BASE_URL}/efetch.fcgi); url.searchParams.set("db", "nuccore"); url.searchParams.set("id", accession); url.searchParams.set("rettype", "fasta"); url.searchParams.set("retmode", "text"); url.searchParams.set("email", this.config.email); url.searchParams.set("tool", this.config.tool); const response = await fetch(url); if (!response.ok) throw new Error(NCBI fetch failed: ${response.status}); const fasta = await response.text(); // Parse FASTA, remove header and newlines return fasta.split("\n").slice(1).join("").toUpperCase(); } /** * Fetch gene annotations in GenBank format */ async fetchAnnotations(accession: string): Promise<GeneAnnotation[]> { const url = new URL(${NCBI_BASE_URL}/efetch.fcgi); url.searchParams.set("db", "nuccore"); url.searchParams.set("id", accession); url.searchParams.set("rettype", "ft"); // Feature table url.searchParams.set("retmode", "text"); url.searchParams.set("email", this.config.email); url.searchParams.set("tool", this.config.tool); const response = await fetch(url); const text = await response.text(); return this.parseFeatureTable(text); } /** * Search for phages by term */ async searchPhages(term: string, maxResults = 20): Promise<string[]> { const url = new URL(${NCBI_BASE_URL}/esearch.fcgi); url.searchParams.set("db", "nuccore"); url.searchParams.set("term", ${term} AND phage[Title]); url.searchParams.set("retmax", String(maxResults)); url.searchParams.set("retmode", "json"); url.searchParams.set("email", this.config.email); const response = await fetch(url); const data = await response.json(); return data.esearchresult.idlist; } private parseFeatureTable(text: string): GeneAnnotation[] { // Parse NCBI feature table format const genes: GeneAnnotation[] = []; const lines = text.split("\n"); let currentGene: Partial | null = null; for (const line of lines) { if (line.startsWith(">Feature")) continue; const match = line.match(/^(\d+)\t(\d+)\t(\w+)/); if (match) { if (currentGene) genes.push(currentGene as GeneAnnotation); currentGene = { start: parseInt(match[1]), end: parseInt(match[2]), type: match[3] }; } else if (currentGene && line.includes("\t\t\t")) { const [, key, value] = line.split("\t\t\t"); if (key === "gene") currentGene.name = value; if (key === "product") currentGene.product = value; } } if (currentGene) genes.push(currentGene as GeneAnnotation); return genes.filter(g => g.type === "CDS" || g.type === "gene"); } } export const ncbiService = new NCBIService(); 3.4 Data Caching Strategy // src/services/cache.ts import { Database } from "bun:sqlite"; class CacheService { private db: Database; constructor(dbPath: string = "./phage-explorer.db") { this.db = new Database(dbPath); this.initSchema(); } private initSchema() { this.db.exec( -- Run schema creation SQL here ); } async cacheGenome(phageId: number, sequence: string): Promise { const CHUNK_SIZE = 10000; // 10kb chunks const chunks = []; for (let i = 0; i < sequence.length; i += CHUNK_SIZE) { chunks.push(sequence.slice(i, i + CHUNK_SIZE)); } const stmt = this.db.prepare( "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO sequences (phage_id, chunk_index, sequence) VALUES (?, ?, ?)" ); const insertChunks = this.db.transaction((chunks: string[]) => { for (let i = 0; i < chunks.length; i++) { stmt.run(phageId, i, chunks[i]); } }); insertChunks(chunks); } getGenome(phageId: number): string { const chunks = this.db .query("SELECT sequence FROM sequences WHERE phage_id = ? ORDER BY chunk_index") .all(phageId) as { sequence: string }[]; return chunks.map(c => c.sequence).join(""); } getGenomeSlice(phageId: number, start: number, end: number): string { const CHUNK_SIZE = 10000; const startChunk = Math.floor(start / CHUNK_SIZE); const endChunk = Math.floor(end / CHUNK_SIZE); const chunks = this.db .query( "SELECT chunk_index, sequence FROM sequences WHERE phage_id = ? AND chunk_index BETWEEN ? AND ? ORDER BY chunk_index" ) .all(phageId, startChunk, endChunk) as { chunk_index: number; sequence: string }[]; const fullSequence = chunks.map(c => c.sequence).join(""); const offset = start - (startChunk * CHUNK_SIZE); return fullSequence.slice(offset, offset + (end - start)); } } export const cacheService = new CacheService(); 4. Core Components 5.1 Main Application Component // src/App.tsx import React, { useEffect } from 'react'; import { Box, Text, useApp, useInput, useStdout } from 'ink'; import { usePhageStore } from './store/phageStore'; import { Header } from './components/Header'; import { PhageInfo } from './components/PhageInfo'; import { SequenceView } from './components/SequenceView'; import { Model3D } from './components/Model3D'; import { GeneMap } from './components/GeneMap'; import { StatusBar } from './components/StatusBar'; import { HelpOverlay } from './components/HelpOverlay'; import { SearchOverlay } from './components/SearchOverlay'; export const App: React.FC = () => { const { stdout } = useStdout(); const { exit } = useApp(); const { currentPhage, phages, currentIndex, showHelp, showSearch, viewMode, showKey, show3DModel, nextPhage, prevPhage, toggleViewMode, toggleHelp, toggleSearch, toggleKey, toggle3DModel, cycleTheme, loadInitialData } = usePhageStore(); // Terminal dimensions const width = stdout?.columns ?? 120; const height = stdout?.rows ?? 40; // Load initial data useEffect(() => { loadInitialData(); }, []); // Keyboard handling useInput((input, key) => { if (showSearch || showHelp) return; if (input === 'q' || input === 'Q') exit(); if (key.downArrow) nextPhage(); if (key.upArrow) prevPhage(); if (input === 'n' || input === 'N') toggleViewMode(); if (input === 'c' || input === 'C') toggleViewMode(); if (input === 'k' || input === 'K') toggleKey(); if (input === 'm' || input === 'M') toggle3DModel(); if (input === 't' || input === 'T') cycleTheme(); if (input === '?' || input === 'h' || input === 'H') toggleHelp(); if (input === 's' || input === 'S' || input === '/') toggleSearch(); }); if (!currentPhage) { return ( ⏳ Loading phage data... ); } return (

<PhageInfo phage={currentPhage} index={currentIndex + 1} total={phages.length} /> {show3DModel && currentPhage.pdbIds?.length > 0 && ( )} {showHelp && } {showSearch && } ); }; 5.2 Zustand State Store // src/store/phageStore.ts import { create } from 'zustand'; import { cacheService } from '../services/cache'; import { ncbiService } from '../services/ncbi'; import { PHAGE_CATALOG } from '../data/catalog'; type ViewMode = 'nucleotide' | 'codon'; type ThemeName = 'classic' | 'ocean' | 'forest' | 'sunset' | 'matrix'; interface Phage { id: number; name: string; accession: string; family: string; host: string; genomeLength: number; gcContent: number; morphology: string; lifecycle: string; description: string; pdbIds?: string[]; } interface PhageState { // Data phages: Phage[]; currentIndex: number; currentPhage: Phage | null; // UI state viewMode: ViewMode; showKey: boolean; show3DModel: boolean; showHelp: boolean; showSearch: boolean; theme: ThemeName; scrollPosition: number; // Actions loadInitialData: () => Promise; nextPhage: () => void; prevPhage: () => void; goToPhage: (index: number) => void; toggleViewMode: () => void; toggleKey: () => void; toggle3DModel: () => void; toggleHelp: () => void; toggleSearch: () => void; cycleTheme: () => void; setScrollPosition: (pos: number) => void; searchPhages: (query: string) => Phage[]; } export const usePhageStore = create((set, get) => ({ // Initial state phages: [], currentIndex: 0, currentPhage: null, viewMode: 'nucleotide', showKey: false, show3DModel: true, showHelp: false, showSearch: false, theme: 'classic', scrollPosition: 0, // Load and cache phage data loadInitialData: async () => { // First, load from cache/catalog const phages = PHAGE_CATALOG.map((p, i) => ({ id: i + 1, ...p, genomeLength: 0, gcContent: 0 })); set({ phages, currentPhage: phages[0], currentIndex: 0 }); // Then fetch genome data for first phage const firstPhage = phages[0]; try { let sequence = cacheService.getGenome(firstPhage.id); if (!sequence) { sequence = await ncbiService.fetchGenome(firstPhage.accession); cacheService.cacheGenome(firstPhage.id, sequence); } // Calculate GC content const gcCount = (sequence.match(/[GC]/gi) || []).length; const gcContent = (gcCount / sequence.length) * 100; set(state => ({ phages: state.phages.map((p, i) => i === 0 ? { ...p, genomeLength: sequence.length, gcContent } : p ), currentPhage: { ...state.currentPhage!, genomeLength: sequence.length, gcContent } })); } catch (error) { console.error('Failed to fetch genome:', error); } }, nextPhage: () => { const { phages, currentIndex } = get(); const newIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % phages.length; set({ currentIndex: newIndex, currentPhage: phages[newIndex], scrollPosition: 0 }); // Pre-fetch next phage genome const nextNextIndex = (newIndex + 1) % phages.length; get().prefetchGenome(phages[nextNextIndex].id, phages[nextNextIndex].accession); }, prevPhage: () => { const { phages, currentIndex } = get(); const newIndex = currentIndex === 0 ? phages.length - 1 : currentIndex - 1; set({ currentIndex: newIndex, currentPhage: phages[newIndex], scrollPosition: 0 }); }, goToPhage: (index: number) => { const { phages } = get(); if (index >= 0 && index < phages.length) { set({ currentIndex: index, currentPhage: phages[index], scrollPosition: 0 }); } }, toggleViewMode: () => { set(state => ({ viewMode: state.viewMode === 'nucleotide' ? 'codon' : 'nucleotide' })); }, toggleKey: () => set(state => ({ showKey: !state.showKey })), toggle3DModel: () => set(state => ({ show3DModel: !state.show3DModel })), toggleHelp: () => set(state => ({ showHelp: !state.showHelp })), toggleSearch: () => set(state => ({ showSearch: !state.showSearch })), cycleTheme: () => { const themes: ThemeName[] = ['classic', 'ocean', 'forest', 'sunset', 'matrix']; set(state => { const currentIdx = themes.indexOf(state.theme); return { theme: themes[(currentIdx + 1) % themes.length] }; }); }, setScrollPosition: (pos: number) => set({ scrollPosition: pos }), searchPhages: (query: string) => { const { phages } = get(); const lowerQuery = query.toLowerCase(); return phages.filter(p => p.name.toLowerCase().includes(lowerQuery) || p.family.toLowerCase().includes(lowerQuery) || p.host.toLowerCase().includes(lowerQuery) || p.accession.toLowerCase().includes(lowerQuery) ); }, // Helper for pre-fetching prefetchGenome: async (phageId: number, accession: string) => { const cached = cacheService.getGenome(phageId); if (!cached) { try { const sequence = await ncbiService.fetchGenome(accession); cacheService.cacheGenome(phageId, sequence); } catch (error) { // Silently fail pre-fetch } } } })); 6. 6.2 Sequence View Component // src/components/SequenceView.tsx import React, { useMemo } from 'react'; import { Box, Text, useStdout } from 'ink'; import { usePhageStore } from '../store/phageStore'; import { cacheService } from '../services/cache'; import { NUCLEOTIDE_THEMES, AMINO_ACID_THEMES, CODON_TABLE, AMINO_ACID_NAMES } from '../themes/nucleotideColors'; interface SequenceViewProps { phageId: number; viewMode: 'nucleotide' | 'codon'; showKey: boolean; } export const SequenceView: React.FC = ({ phageId, viewMode, showKey }) => { const { stdout } = useStdout(); const { theme, scrollPosition, setScrollPosition } = usePhageStore(); // Calculate available dimensions const width = (stdout?.columns ?? 120) - 4; // Account for borders const height = (stdout?.rows ?? 40) - 12; // Account for header/footer const keyWidth = showKey ? 24 : 0; const sequenceWidth = width - keyWidth - 2; // Nucleotides per row (for nucleotide view) const charsPerRow = sequenceWidth; // Amino acids per row (for codon view - 3 nucleotides = 1 AA displayed with spacing) const aasPerRow = Math.floor(sequenceWidth / 3); const visibleRows = height - 2; // Account for view header // Get sequence data const sequence = useMemo(() => { const startPos = scrollPosition; const endPos = viewMode === 'nucleotide' ? startPos + (charsPerRow * visibleRows) : startPos + (aasPerRow * 3 * visibleRows); return cacheService.getGenomeSlice(phageId, startPos, endPos); }, [phageId, scrollPosition, viewMode, charsPerRow, aasPerRow, visibleRows]); // Render nucleotide sequence const renderNucleotideView = () => { const nucTheme = NUCLEOTIDE_THEMES[theme] || NUCLEOTIDE_THEMES.classic; const rows: React.ReactNode[] = []; for (let row = 0; row < visibleRows && row * charsPerRow < sequence.length; row++) { const rowStart = row * charsPerRow; const rowSeq = sequence.slice(rowStart, rowStart + charsPerRow); const coloredChars = rowSeq.split('').map((char, i) => { const colors = nucTheme[char as keyof NucleotideTheme] || nucTheme.N; return ( {char} ); }); rows.push( {coloredChars} ); } return rows; }; // Render codon/amino acid view const renderCodonView = () => { const aaTheme = AMINO_ACID_THEMES[theme] || AMINO_ACID_THEMES.classic; const rows: React.ReactNode[] = []; // Translate to amino acids const aminoAcids: string[] = []; for (let i = 0; i < sequence.length - 2; i += 3) { const codon = sequence.slice(i, i + 3); aminoAcids.push(CODON_TABLE[codon] || '?'); } for (let row = 0; row < visibleRows && row * aasPerRow < aminoAcids.length; row++) { const rowStart = row * aasPerRow; const rowAAs = aminoAcids.slice(rowStart, rowStart + aasPerRow); const coloredAAs = rowAAs.map((aa, i) => { const colors = aaTheme[aa as keyof AminoAcidTheme] || { fg: '#FFFFFF', bg: '#666666' }; return ( { ${aa} } ); }); rows.push( {coloredAAs} ); } return rows; }; // Render amino acid key const renderKey = () => { if (!showKey) return null; const aaTheme = AMINO_ACID_THEMES[theme] || AMINO_ACID_THEMES.classic; const entries = Object.entries(AMINO_ACID_NAMES); return ( Amino Acids {entries.map(([code, name]) => { const colors = aaTheme[code as keyof AminoAcidTheme]; return ( {code} {name} ); })} ); }; const modeLabel = viewMode === 'nucleotide' ? '[N] Nucleotide' : '[C] Codon'; const currentPos = scrollPosition + 1; const endPos = Math.min( scrollPosition + (viewMode === 'nucleotide' ? charsPerRow * visibleRows : aasPerRow * 3 * visibleRows), cacheService.getGenome(phageId).length ); const totalLength = cacheService.getGenome(phageId).length || '...'; return ( ━━━ SEQUENCE VIEW {modeLabel} ━━━ {viewMode === 'nucleotide' ? renderNucleotideView() : renderCodonView()} Position: {currentPos.toLocaleString()}-{endPos.toLocaleString()} of {totalLength.toLocaleString()} [←→] Scroll [G] GoTo {showKey && viewMode === 'codon' && renderKey()} ); }; 6.3 Virtualized Rendering for Large Genomes // src/utils/virtualizer.ts interface VirtualWindow { startIndex: number; endIndex: number; overscan: number; } export class SequenceVirtualizer { private totalLength: number; private viewportSize: number; private overscan: number; constructor(totalLength: number, viewportSize: number, overscan = 100) { this.totalLength = totalLength; this.viewportSize = viewportSize; this.overscan = overscan; } getWindow(scrollPosition: number): VirtualWindow { const startIndex = Math.max(0, scrollPosition - this.overscan); const endIndex = Math.min( this.totalLength, scrollPosition + this.viewportSize + this.overscan ); return { startIndex, endIndex, overscan: this.overscan }; } /** * Pre-compute positions for smooth scrolling */ getJumpPoints(interval = 1000): number[] { const points: number[] = []; for (let i = 0; i < this.totalLength; i += interval) { points.push(i); } return points; } /** * Find nearest gene start position */ snapToGene(position: number, genes: GeneAnnotation[]): number { let nearest = genes[0]?.start || 0; let minDistance = Math.abs(position - nearest); for (const gene of genes) { const distance = Math.abs(position - gene.start); if (distance < minDistance) { minDistance = distance; nearest = gene.start; } } return nearest; } } 7. 3D Model Rendering 7.1 ASCII/Braille 3D Renderer // src/3d/asciiRenderer.ts /** * Renders 3D models as ASCII/Braille art for terminal display * Uses simple ray marching and shading */ // Braille patterns for sub-character resolution (2x4 dots per character) const BRAILLE_BASE = 0x2800; const BRAILLE_DOTS = [ [0x01, 0x08], // Row 0 [0x02, 0x10], // Row 1 [0x04, 0x20], // Row 2 [0x40, 0x80] // Row 3 ]; // ASCII density ramp for shading const ASCII_RAMP = ' .:-=+*#%@'; const ASCII_RAMP_EXTENDED = ' .\':!^"~-_,;<=+?/\\|)(}{][*&#%@'; interface Vec3 { x: number; y: number; z: number; } interface Triangle { v1: Vec3; v2: Vec3; v3: Vec3; normal: Vec3; } interface Mesh { triangles: Triangle[]; bounds: { min: Vec3; max: Vec3 }; } export class AsciiRenderer { private width: number; private height: number; private zBuffer: number[][]; private frameBuffer: string[][]; private lightDir: Vec3 = { x: -0.5, y: 0.5, z: 1 }; constructor(width: number, height: number) { this.width = width; this.height = height; this.zBuffer = Array(height).fill(null).map(() => Array(width).fill(Infinity)); this.frameBuffer = Array(height).fill(null).map(() => Array(width).fill(' ')); } /** * Load OBJ file format */ loadOBJ(objContent: string): Mesh { const vertices: Vec3[] = []; const triangles: Triangle[] = []; const lines = objContent.split('\n'); for (const line of lines) { const parts = line.trim().split(/\s+/); if (parts[0] === 'v') { vertices.push({ x: parseFloat(parts[1]), y: parseFloat(parts[2]), z: parseFloat(parts[3]) }); } else if (parts[0] === 'f') { // Parse face (1-indexed in OBJ) const indices = parts.slice(1).map(p => parseInt(p.split('/')[0]) - 1); // Triangulate if quad for (let i = 1; i < indices.length - 1; i++) { const v1 = vertices[indices[0]]; const v2 = vertices[indices[i]]; const v3 = vertices[indices[i + 1]]; // Calculate normal const normal = this.calculateNormal(v1, v2, v3); triangles.push({ v1, v2, v3, normal }); } } } const bounds = this.calculateBounds(vertices); return { triangles, bounds }; } /** * Calculate triangle normal */ private calculateNormal(v1: Vec3, v2: Vec3, v3: Vec3): Vec3 { const u = { x: v2.x - v1.x, y: v2.y - v1.y, z: v2.z - v1.z }; const v = { x: v3.x - v1.x, y: v3.y - v1.y, z: v3.z - v1.z }; const normal = { x: u.y * v.z - u.z * v.y, y: u.z * v.x - u.x * v.z, z: u.x * v.y - u.y * v.x }; // Normalize const len = Math.sqrt(normal.x ** 2 + normal.y ** 2 + normal.z ** 2); return { x: normal.x / len, y: normal.y / len, z: normal.z / len }; } private calculateBounds(vertices: Vec3[]): { min: Vec3; max: Vec3 } { const min = { x: Infinity, y: Infinity, z: Infinity }; const max = { x: -Infinity, y: -Infinity, z: -Infinity }; for (const v of vertices) { min.x = Math.min(min.x, v.x); min.y = Math.min(min.y, v.y); min.z = Math.min(min.z, v.z); max.x = Math.max(max.x, v.x); max.y = Math.max(max.y, v.y); max.z = Math.max(max.z, v.z); } return { min, max }; } /** * Apply rotation matrix */ private rotate(point: Vec3, angleX: number, angleY: number): Vec3 { // Rotate around Y axis let x = point.x * Math.cos(angleY) - point.z * Math.sin(angleY); let z = point.x * Math.sin(angleY) + point.z * Math.cos(angleY); // Rotate around X axis let y = point.y * Math.cos(angleX) - z * Math.sin(angleX); z = point.y * Math.sin(angleX) + z * Math.cos(angleX); return { x, y, z }; } /** * Project 3D point to 2D screen */ private project(point: Vec3, bounds: { min: Vec3; max: Vec3 }): { x: number; y: number; z: number } { // Center and normalize to bounds const size = { x: bounds.max.x - bounds.min.x, y: bounds.max.y - bounds.min.y, z: bounds.max.z - bounds.min.z }; const maxSize = Math.max(size.x, size.y, size.z); const scale = Math.min(this.width, this.height * 2) / (maxSize * 1.2); const centered = { x: point.x - (bounds.min.x + bounds.max.x) / 2, y: point.y - (bounds.min.y + bounds.max.y) / 2, z: point.z - (bounds.min.z + bounds.max.z) / 2 }; // Simple perspective projection const perspective = 3; const z = centered.z + perspective; const factor = perspective / z; return { x: Math.floor(this.width / 2 + centered.x * scale * factor), y: Math.floor(this.height / 2 - centered.y * scale * factor * 0.5), // Aspect correction z: centered.z }; } /** * Render mesh to ASCII frame */ render(mesh: Mesh, angleX: number, angleY: number): string[] { // Clear buffers for (let y = 0; y < this.height; y++) { for (let x = 0; x < this.width; x++) { this.zBuffer[y][x] = Infinity; this.frameBuffer[y][x] = ' '; } } // Render each triangle for (const tri of mesh.triangles) { // Rotate vertices const v1 = this.rotate(tri.v1, angleX, angleY); const v2 = this.rotate(tri.v2, angleX, angleY); const v3 = this.rotate(tri.v3, angleX, angleY); const normal = this.rotate(tri.normal, angleX, angleY); // Back-face culling if (normal.z < 0) continue; // Project to 2D const p1 = this.project(v1, mesh.bounds); const p2 = this.project(v2, mesh.bounds); const p3 = this.project(v3, mesh.bounds); // Calculate lighting const rotatedLight = this.rotate(this.lightDir, -angleX, -angleY); let brightness = Math.max(0, normal.x * rotatedLight.x + normal.y * rotatedLight.y + normal.z * rotatedLight.z ); // Get ASCII character for brightness const charIndex = Math.floor(brightness * (ASCII_RAMP.length - 1)); const char = ASCII_RAMP[charIndex]; // Rasterize triangle (scanline algorithm) this.rasterizeTriangle(p1, p2, p3, char); } // Convert frame buffer to strings return this.frameBuffer.map(row => row.join('')); } /** * Rasterize a single triangle */ private rasterizeTriangle( p1: { x: number; y: number; z: number }, p2: { x: number; y: number; z: number }, p3: { x: number; y: number; z: number }, char: string ) { // Sort by Y coordinate const points = [p1, p2, p3].sort((a, b) => a.y - b.y); const [top, mid, bot] = points; // Scanline fill for (let y = Math.max(0, top.y); y <= Math.min(this.height - 1, bot.y); y++) { let xStart: number, xEnd: number; if (y < mid.y) { xStart = this.lerp(top.x, mid.x, (y - top.y) / (mid.y - top.y || 1)); xEnd = this.lerp(top.x, bot.x, (y - top.y) / (bot.y - top.y || 1)); } else { xStart = this.lerp(mid.x, bot.x, (y - mid.y) / (bot.y - mid.y || 1)); xEnd = this.lerp(top.x, bot.x, (y - top.y) / (bot.y - top.y || 1)); } if (xStart > xEnd) [xStart, xEnd] = [xEnd, xStart]; for (let x = Math.max(0, Math.floor(xStart)); x <= Math.min(this.width - 1, Math.floor(xEnd)); x++) { // Simple z-interpolation const z = (p1.z + p2.z + p3.z) / 3; if (z < this.zBuffer[y][x]) { this.zBuffer[y][x] = z; this.frameBuffer[y][x] = char; } } } } private lerp(a: number, b: number, t: number): number { return a + (b - a) * t; } /** * Pre-render animation frames */ preRenderAnimation(mesh: Mesh, frames: number): string[][] { const renderedFrames: string[][] = []; for (let i = 0; i < frames; i++) { const angle = (i / frames) * Math.PI * 2; renderedFrames.push(this.render(mesh, Math.PI / 6, angle)); } return renderedFrames; } } 7.2 3D Model Component // src/components/Model3D.tsx import React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react'; import { Box, Text } from 'ink'; import { AsciiRenderer } from '../3d/asciiRenderer'; import { pdbService } from '../services/pdb'; interface Model3DProps { pdbId: string; width?: number; height?: number; } export const Model3D: React.FC = ({ pdbId, width = 20, height = 16 }) => { const [frames, setFrames] = useState<string[][]>([]); const [currentFrame, setCurrentFrame] = useState(0); const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true); const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null); useEffect(() => { let cancelled = false; const loadModel = async () => { try { setLoading(true); setError(null); // Try to load from cache first let objData = await pdbService.getCachedModel(pdbId); if (!objData) { // Fetch from PDB and convert const pdbData = await pdbService.fetchPDB(pdbId); objData = pdbService.pdbToSimpleOBJ(pdbData); await pdbService.cacheModel(pdbId, objData); } if (cancelled) return; // Render animation frames const renderer = new AsciiRenderer(width, height); const mesh = renderer.loadOBJ(objData); const animationFrames = renderer.preRenderAnimation(mesh, 36); // 10° increments setFrames(animationFrames); setLoading(false); } catch (err) { if (!cancelled) { setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to load model'); setLoading(false); } } }; loadModel(); return () => { cancelled = true; }; }, [pdbId, width, height]); // Animation loop useEffect(() => { if (frames.length === 0) return; const interval = setInterval(() => { setCurrentFrame(f => (f + 1) % frames.length); }, 100); // ~10 FPS rotation return () => clearInterval(interval); }, [frames.length]); if (loading) { return ( Loading 3D Model... ); } if (error || frames.length === 0) { return ( No 3D Model ); } const frame = frames[currentFrame]; return ( 3D MODEL {frame.map((line, i) => ( {line} ))} PDB: {pdbId} ); }; 7.3 PDB Service // src/services/pdb.ts const PDB_BASE_URL = "https://files.rcsb.org/download"; class PDBService { async fetchPDB(pdbId: string): Promise { const url = ${PDB_BASE_URL}/${pdbId.toUpperCase()}.pdb; const response = await fetch(url); if (!response.ok) throw new Error(PDB fetch failed: ${response.status}); return response.text(); } /** * Convert PDB format to simplified OBJ for rendering * Extracts only CA (alpha carbon) atoms for a simplified backbone view */ pdbToSimpleOBJ(pdbContent: string): string { const atoms: { x: number; y: number; z: number }[] = []; const lines = pdbContent.split('\n'); for (const line of lines) { // Only get CA atoms for backbone if (line.startsWith('ATOM') && line.substring(12, 16).trim() === 'CA') { const x = parseFloat(line.substring(30, 38)); const y = parseFloat(line.substring(38, 46)); const z = parseFloat(line.substring(46, 54)); atoms.push({ x, y, z }); } } if (atoms.length === 0) { // Fallback: get all atoms for (const line of lines) { if (line.startsWith('ATOM') || line.startsWith('HETATM')) { const x = parseFloat(line.substring(30, 38)); const y = parseFloat(line.substring(38, 46)); const z = parseFloat(line.substring(46, 54)); atoms.push({ x, y, z }); } } } // Generate OBJ content let obj = '# Converted from PDB\n'; // Vertices for (const atom of atoms) { obj += v ${atom.x} ${atom.y} ${atom.z}\n; } // Create simple connectivity (connect sequential CA atoms as lines/ribbons) // For visualization, create simple triangles between nearby atoms for (let i = 0; i < atoms.length - 2; i++) { obj += f ${i + 1} ${i + 2} ${i + 3}\n; } return obj; } // Cache methods using the database async getCachedModel(pdbId: string): Promise<string | null> { // Implementation uses SQLite cache return null; // Placeholder } async cacheModel(pdbId: string, objData: string): Promise { // Implementation uses SQLite cache } } export const pdbService = new PDBService(); borderFocus: string; success: string; warning: string; error: string; }; nucleotides: NucleotideTheme; aminoAcids: AminoAcidTheme; } export const THEMES: Record<string, Theme> = { classic: { name: 'Classic', colors: { primary: '#00FFFF', secondary: '#FF00FF', accent: '#FFFF00', background: '#000000', text: '#FFFFFF', textDim: '#888888', border: '#444444', borderFocus: '#00FFFF', success: '#00FF00', warning: '#FFFF00', error: '#FF0000' }, nucleotides: NUCLEOTIDE_THEMES.classic, aminoAcids: AMINO_ACID_THEMES.classic }, ocean: { name: 'Ocean', colors: { primary: '#00B4D8', secondary: '#0077B6', accent: '#90E0EF', background: '#03045E', text: '#CAF0F8', textDim: '#48CAE4', border: '#023E8A', borderFocus: '#00B4D8', success: '#48CAE4', warning: '#F9C74F', error: '#E63946' }, nucleotides: NUCLEOTIDE_THEMES.ocean, aminoAcids: AMINO_ACID_THEMES.classic }, forest: { name: 'Forest', colors: { primary: '#52B788', secondary: '#2D6A4F', accent: '#95D5B2', background: '#081C15', text: '#D8F3DC', textDim: '#74C69D', border: '#1B4332', borderFocus: '#52B788', success: '#40916C', warning: '#E9C46A', error: '#E76F51' }, nucleotides: NUCLEOTIDE_THEMES.forest, aminoAcids: AMINO_ACID_THEMES.classic }, sunset: { name: 'Sunset', colors: { primary: '#F77F00', secondary: '#D62828', accent: '#FCBF49', background: '#1D1128', text: '#FEFAE0', textDim: '#DDA15E', border: '#3D348B', borderFocus: '#F77F00', success: '#7CB518', warning: '#FCBF49', error: '#D62828' }, nucleotides: NUCLEOTIDE_THEMES.sunset, aminoAcids: AMINO_ACID_THEMES.classic }, matrix: { name: 'Matrix', colors: { primary: '#00FF00', secondary: '#00CC00', accent: '#00FF00', background: '#000000', text: '#00FF00', textDim: '#006600', border: '#003300', borderFocus: '#00FF00', success: '#00FF00', warning: '#CCFF00', error: '#FF0000' }, nucleotides: NUCLEOTIDE_THEMES.matrix, aminoAcids: AMINO_ACID_THEMES.classic } }; Keyboard Navigation Complete Keyboard Map Key Action Context ↓ Next phage Main view ↑ Previous phage Main view ← Scroll sequence left Main view → Scroll sequence right Main view Page Up Large scroll up Sequence view Page Down Large scroll down Sequence view Home Go to sequence start Sequence view End Go to sequence end Sequence view N Toggle Nucleotide view Main view C Toggle Codon/Amino acid view Main view K Toggle amino acid key Codon view M Toggle 3D model Main view T Cycle color theme Main view G Go to position dialog Main view S or / Open search Main view ? or H Toggle help Main view Q Quit application Any Escape Close overlay/dialog Overlays Enter Confirm selection Dialogs 1-9 Quick jump to gene Main view [ Previous gene boundary Sequence view ] Next gene boundary Sequence view Input Handling // src/hooks/useKeyboard.ts import { useInput, useApp } from 'ink'; import { usePhageStore } from '../store/phageStore'; import { cacheService } from '../services/cache'; export const useKeyboard = () => { const { exit } = useApp(); const store = usePhageStore(); useInput((input, key) => { // Global shortcuts (always active) if (input === 'q' || input === 'Q') { exit(); return; } // Handle overlays first if (store.showHelp || store.showSearch) { if (key.escape) { store.showHelp ? store.toggleHelp() : store.toggleSearch(); } return; } // Navigation if (key.downArrow) { store.nextPhage(); } else if (key.upArrow) { store.prevPhage(); } else if (key.leftArrow) { store.setScrollPosition(Math.max(0, store.scrollPosition - 100)); } else if (key.rightArrow) { const genome = cacheService.getGenome(store.currentPhage!.id); store.setScrollPosition(Math.min(genome.length - 100, store.scrollPosition + 100)); } else if (key.pageUp) { store.setScrollPosition(Math.max(0, store.scrollPosition - 1000)); } else if (key.pageDown) { const genome = cacheService.getGenome(store.currentPhage!.id); store.setScrollPosition(Math.min(genome.length - 100, store.scrollPosition + 1000)); } // View toggles if (input === 'n' || input === 'N' || input === 'c' || input === 'C') { store.toggleViewMode(); } else if (input === 'k' || input === 'K') { store.toggleKey(); } else if (input === 'm' || input === 'M') { store.toggle3DModel(); } else if (input === 't' || input === 'T') { store.cycleTheme(); } // Dialogs if (input === '?' || input === 'h' || input === 'H') { store.toggleHelp(); } else if (input === 's' || input === 'S' || input === '/') { store.toggleSearch(); } else if (input === 'g' || input === 'G') { store.toggleGoTo(); } // Gene navigation if (input === '[') { // Previous gene const genes = store.currentGenes; const prevGene = genes .filter(g => g.start < store.scrollPosition) .sort((a, b) => b.start - a.start)[0]; if (prevGene) store.setScrollPosition(prevGene.start); } else if (input === ']') { // Next gene const genes = store.currentGenes; const nextGene = genes .filter(g => g.start > store.scrollPosition) .sort((a, b) => a.start - b.start)[0]; if (nextGene) store.setScrollPosition(nextGene.start); } // Number keys for quick gene jump const num = parseInt(input); if (!isNaN(num) && num >= 1 && num <= 9) { const genes = store.currentGenes; if (genes[num - 1]) { store.setScrollPosition(genes[num - 1].start); } } }); }; 10. Browser Deployment (ghostty-web) 10.1 Architecture for Browser ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Browser Environment │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ │ │ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ ghostty-web Terminal │ │ │ │ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ │ │ React/Ink TUI │ │ │ │ │ │ (Rendered as ANSI escape codes) │ │ │ │ │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ │ ▼ │ │ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ sql.js (SQLite WASM) │ │ │ │ Data persistence via OPFS │ │ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ │ ▼ │ │ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ NCBI/PDB APIs (fetch from browser) │ │ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ 10.2 Browser Entry Point // src/browser/index.ts import { init, Terminal } from 'ghostty-web'; import initSqlJs from 'sql.js'; import { renderToTerminal } from './terminalRenderer'; import { App } from '../App'; async function initBrowserApp() { // Initialize ghostty-web await init(); // Create terminal const term = new Terminal({ fontSize: 14, fontFamily: 'JetBrains Mono, Consolas, monospace', theme: { background: '#0a0a0a', foreground: '#e0e0e0', cursor: '#00ffff', selectionBackground: '#44444480' } }); // Mount to DOM const container = document.getElementById('terminal'); if (!container) throw new Error('Terminal container not found'); term.open(container); term.focus(); // Initialize SQLite WASM const SQL = await initSqlJs({ locateFile: file => https://sql.js.org/dist/${file} }); // Try to load persisted database from OPFS const db = await loadOrCreateDatabase(SQL); // Initialize and render our Ink app to the terminal await renderToTerminal(term, App, { db }); console.log('Phage Explorer initialized in browser mode'); } async function loadOrCreateDatabase(SQL: any) { // Check for OPFS support if ('storage' in navigator && 'getDirectory' in navigator.storage) { try { const root = await navigator.storage.getDirectory(); const fileHandle = await root.getFileHandle('phage-explorer.db', { create: true }); const file = await fileHandle.getFile(); const buffer = await file.arrayBuffer(); if (buffer.byteLength > 0) { return new SQL.Database(new Uint8Array(buffer)); } } catch (e) { console.warn('OPFS not available, using in-memory database'); } } // Create new in-memory database const db = new SQL.Database(); initializeSchema(db); return db; } function initializeSchema(db: any) { db.run( CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS phages ( id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, name TEXT NOT NULL, accession TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, -- ... rest of schema ); -- ... rest of tables ); } // Entry point initBrowserApp().catch(console.error); 10.3 Terminal Renderer Bridge // src/browser/terminalRenderer.ts import React from 'react'; import { render } from 'ink'; import { Terminal } from 'ghostty-web'; interface RenderOptions { db: any; [key: string]: any; } /** * Bridge between Ink and ghostty-web * Captures Ink's stdout output and writes to ghostty-web terminal */ export async function renderToTerminal( term: Terminal, AppComponent: React.ComponentType, options: RenderOptions ) { // Create a mock stdout stream that writes to the terminal const mockStdout = { columns: term.cols || 120, rows: term.rows || 40, write: (data: string) => { term.write(data); }, on: () => {}, off: () => {}, isTTY: true }; // Create mock stdin for input handling const mockStdin = createInputBridge(term); // Create the React element with context const element = React.createElement(AppComponent, { ...options, terminal: term }); // Render with Ink const { rerender, unmount, waitUntilExit } = render(element, { stdout: mockStdout as any, stdin: mockStdin as any, patchConsole: false, exitOnCtrlC: false }); // Handle terminal resize term.onResize(({ cols, rows }) => { mockStdout.columns = cols; mockStdout.rows = rows; rerender(React.createElement(AppComponent, { ...options, terminal: term })); }); return { rerender, unmount, waitUntilExit }; } function createInputBridge(term: Terminal) { const listeners: ((data: string) => void)[] = []; term.onData((data: string) => { for (const listener of listeners) { listener(data); } }); return { isTTY: true, isRaw: true, setRawMode: () => {}, on: (event: string, callback: (data: string) => void) => { if (event === 'data') { listeners.push(callback); } }, off: (event: string, callback: (data: string) => void) => { if (event === 'data') { const idx = listeners.indexOf(callback); if (idx >= 0) listeners.splice(idx, 1); } } }; } 10.4 Browser HTML Template Phage Explorer <style> * { margin: 0; padding: 0; box-sizing: border-box; } html, body { height: 100%; overflow: hidden; background: #0a0a0a; } #terminal { width: 100%; height: 100%; } /* Loading screen */ #loading { position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; background: #0a0a0a; color: #00ffff; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; z-index: 1000; } #loading.hidden { display: none; } .spinner { width: 40px; height: 40px; border: 3px solid #333; border-top-color: #00ffff; border-radius: 50%; animation: spin 1s linear infinite; } @keyframes spin { to { transform: rotate(360deg); Performance Optimizations 13.1 Sequence Rendering // Memoize colored character generation const useColoredSequence = ( sequence: string, theme: string, viewMode: ViewMode ) => { return useMemo(() => { const colors = viewMode === 'nucleotide' ? NUCLEOTIDE_THEMES[theme] : AMINO_ACID_THEMES[theme]; // Pre-compute all colored chars for visible window return sequence.split('').map(char => ({ char, ...colors[char as keyof typeof colors] || { fg: '#888', bg: '#000' } })); }, [sequence, theme, viewMode]); }; 13.2 Pre-fetching Strategy // Background data loading const prefetchManager = { queue: new Set(), active: false, enqueue(accession: string) { this.queue.add(accession); this.process(); }, async process() { if (this.active || this.queue.size === 0) return; this.active = true; const accession = this.queue.values().next().value; this.queue.delete(accession); try { await ncbiService.fetchGenome(accession); } catch (e) { // Silently fail } this.active = false; this.process(); } }; 13.3 Chunked Database Access // Only load visible window + overscan const getVisibleSequence = ( phageId: number, scrollPos: number, viewportSize: number ) => { const OVERSCAN = 500; const start = Math.max(0, scrollPos - OVERSCAN); const end = scrollPos + viewportSize + OVERSCAN; return cacheService.getGenomeSlice(phageId, start, end); }; 14.
